highlights.title: Explore the globe in field recordings
highlights.summary: I love field recordings. I love making them. I love them when they're incorporated into my ambient music. They're great background noise for working or sleeping. But they're also great for active listening, focusing in on the fine nuances of burbling brooks or urban chaos.
body: Earth Garden takes you around the world using environmental audio from Freesound.

The recordings are all pulled from Freesound, which does mean quality can vary, and volume between clips can be inconsistent. It also means that recordings tend to be more concentrated in the US and Europe, especially the UK. But it’s still quite fun and soothing to set the globe to rotate automatically, and as the reticle nears points on the Earth, it transitions to those new sounds. You can even click a button to put some generic ambient drones in the background.

highlights.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
highlights.summary: The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."
body: Three hikers were rescued from California’s Mount Shasta this week after using Google’s AI chatbot Gemini to plan their expedition, according to the Chicago Tribune.

A report from the Siskiyou County sheriff’s office said that three young men set off on their hike at 3am and — although hikers are told to turn around if they haven’t reached the summit by noon — they made it to the top at 7pm.

The trio then tried to descend in the dark, called the sheriff’s office to ask for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before being rescued the next morning by Forest Service rangers and volunteers.

“It is always advisable to call the local USFS Mount Shasta ranger station ahead of your trip to ensure you have the most accurate information, and to never rely solely on AI for your trip planning,” the sheriff’s office said.

body: Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.
The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic vs the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot.
"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

body: This year marks the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda, and it’s finally time to get the party started. On Tuesday, Sept. 8, Nintendo will host The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct. The 30-minute stream promises to “deliver a variety of The Legend of Zelda related information.” That’s a bit of a clinical description, but the vague wording makes sense when you consider what Nintendo could reveal during the stream.

The main event of this showcase is undoubtedly The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Nintendo has said next to nothing about its Switch 2 remake since it was first teased, even though it’s supposed to launch sometime in the next few months. Expect a blowout here that gives us a real look at the visuals, a deep dive into gameplay, and a release date. Nintendo might save a few of the finer details for its Treehouse stream the next day, but all the major bullet points should be here.

highlights.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
highlights.summary: OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.
body: In a post on X, OpenAI said it previously “treated misalignment [when AI models and agents pursue goals different from those of their creators and users] largely as a research question, which gets communicated in research publications.” But as misalignment has “caused new types of real-world impact,” the company said its approach needs “to expand for this new phase of model capabilities.”

A company spokesperson told Reuters that OpenAI could not “meaningfully respond to claims or findings on a report that we have not had an opportunity to review,” but they insisted that the company’s legal team had not discouraged an investigation.

In its more recent social media post, OpenAI said it had considered the “wiki incident” to be “an instance of misalignment similar” to others that it had already shared. The company contrasted this with “the Hugging Face incident,” where it “followed a traditional security incident response playbook.”

highlights.title: 'The Gentlemen' Season 3 Confirmed? Potential Release Date, and Everything You Need to Know
highlights.summary: Season 2 of Guy Ritchie ’s stylish crime drama The Gentlemen was released on Netflix on Sept. 3. It’s easy to binge the eight episodes, which are packed with chase scenes, bloody shootouts, gorgeous sets, and convoluted schemes.
body: Yes! Netflix and Ritchie announced that the show had been renewed in August, about a week before the season 2 premiere.

In The Gentlemen season 1, Eddie returns home from serving as a United Nations peacekeeping officer after his father’s death and learns that a marijuana grow house was operating on his family’s estate. After initially trying to clear his debt to the gang leader Bobby Glass (Ray Winstone), Eddie decides to get deeper into the drug game as a way to restore his estate to its former glory.

That leads to a series of questionable schemes in season 2. Eddie becomes a hereditary peer in the House of Lords in the hopes of passing legislation to decriminalize marijuana, even though Glass wants to kill the bill. He borrows money from Italian mob boss Marco Moretti (Sergio Castellitto) to fund the expansion and winds up having to leverage his estate as collateral to get a loan from the billionaire Fred Johnston (Giancarlo Esposito) to pay Moretti back when the vote fails. Bobby, in turn, buys the debt from Johnston to gain more control over Eddie, who he believes is “evolving” into a worthy inheritor of his drug empire.

highlights.title: Australia’s first fashion library’s rule for borrowers? No stylists allowed
highlights.summary: Being able to touch and examine garments in person can be a vital source of inspiration for designers. Now a collection which does just that has relocated from Europe to Melbourne. In what was once a nun’s bedroom, a long-sleeved, slate-blue Hermès dress from the 1970s hangs beside a window.
body: The private collection of fashion items, amassed over a decade of travel, is available for rent by designers and fashion students seeking inspiration. Its curator and owner, fashion designer Hannah Canham, has lived and worked across North America (in New York and Los Angeles) and Europe (in Madrid, Berlin, London and Paris) where designer archives are commonplace.

She has been running the archive since 2018, but in 2024 she returned home to Melbourne with her treasure trove of approximately 1,000 pieces in tow. She reopened the archive for commercial use in March. While museum and educational institutions already house garment collections, This Era Archive is the first of its kind in Australia.

“In Australia it’s new information for some designers,” Canham says. “Whereas working in Europe, this is part of their design process. They start each season by looking for inspiration, going to museums, reading old books and going to archives.”
There are two ideas at the heart of the project: that fashion is self-referential and cyclical; and that the best design needs to be touched to be properly understood.

highlights.title: Architecting memory and storage in the AI era
highlights.summary: The era of AI inference has arrived. Imagine a healthcare system analyzing millions of data points in real time to accelerate life-saving medical research, or an intelligent assistant instantly resolving thousands of complex customer needs at once.
body: This shift changes what infrastructure must deliver. Performance, latency, memory bandwidth, storage throughput, and networking cannot be optimized in silos. Inference workloads are continuous, geographically distributed, and highly sensitive to response time, requiring systems designed for scale, resilience, and efficiency from the start.

“We tend to think of AI as a single workload, and it’s not. It’s thousands, it’s millions, it’s billions of different workloads,” says Jim McGregor, founder and principal analyst, Tirias Research. AI inference changes the optimization problem from one of raw compute to coordinated infrastructure—memory, storage, and networking.

For business leaders, the priority is clear: AI infrastructure decisions must balance cost, flexibility, and future readiness. The winners will be organizations that improve performance per watt, reduce environmental footprint, and remove memory and storage bottlenecks before they limit growth.

highlights.title: Zach Cregger Says He's Done With Franchise Films After Resident Evil
highlights.summary: Resident Evil movie director Zach Cregger is days away from his survival horror adaptation's theatrical premiere, but don't expect to help bring another franchise film to the big screen ever again.
body: The filmmaker behind this month's Capcom project talked about what's next for him during a conversation with Deadline. When asked if he's ever been pressured to spearhead another recognizable IP, he gave a blunt answer: "I'm not doing that."

"I have never been approached by another franchise," Cregger said. "Maybe I have, but it would never get to me because I have been very clear that I’m not doing that. I’m doing this, and that’s it for me."

One might suspect Cregger's aversion to big franchise films like Resident Evil might stem from the backlash he's received in the months leading up to his movie's premiere. While the Barbarian and Weapons creator certainly has plenty of defenders looking forward to seeing his new live-action take, there have been many, many others who aren't quite as excited.

Most of the pressure has come from those who feel his Resident Evil doesn't align with the game it's based on. Changes to the source material, including its modern setting and snowy Raccoon City, have set fans on edge, while others aren't in love with the idea of following a new protagonist (Austin Abrams' Bryan Hodukavich) instead of someone like Leon S. Kennedy or Claire Redfield.

highlights.title: Hey, Oscars: No Sympathy Required to Give Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ the Consideration It Deserves
highlights.summary: Let’s dispense with the suspense. Mike Leigh has been nominated for an Academy Award seven times and has won it zero times. That seems wrong. He has a Palme d’Or, a Golden Lion, five decades of films that taught generations of actors what unglamorous truth looks like and one of the most distinctive…
body: That makes the season’s obvious question unavoidable: What should the Academy do with Mike Leigh’s final film? The answer is not — give him an Oscar because he is 83.

“Tender Loving Care” does not need a sympathy campaign. It is vintage Leigh — wry, melancholy, humane, alert to the small emotional humiliations that become, over the course of a life, the events that define us. Kate O’Flynn’s Amy anchors it — an Emmy nominee for “Widow’s Bay,” and when the trophies are handed out Sept. 14, very possibly a winner — a social worker steadying a father in decline, gutted by a breakup and kept upright by wine and by Rosie, the live-wire best friend played exquisitely by Alice Bailey Johnson. Marion Bailey, as Amy’s mother, has already emerged from Telluride as a standout, a veteran thespian never given her proper due.

highlights.title: Roland is getting into generative AI music with Melody Flip
highlights.summary: It's not quite the "push button; get song" of Suno, but Roland's new Melody Flip tool marks the company's foray into generative AI music. Available as a plug-in for your digital audio workstation (DAW), Melody Flip offers around 250 "Palettes," which are essentially themed collections of musical…
body: Rather than fully polished tracks, the plugin is supposed to act as a creative spark.

The sound selection is further proof that you’re not supposed to use Melody Flip outputs out of the box. The presets available are mostly the sort of general MIDI tones you’d find in ‘90s video games. It seems like the intended use is to export the MIDI data from Melody Flip directly into your DAW to manipulate and pair with other, more powerful synth plugins.

After years of seeming lost in the woods and alienating customers with its messy Roland Cloud subscription service, the company was back on track recently. The P-6 Creative Sampler, SH-4d, and Gaia 2 synth all addressed major issues with the company’s lineup. And Roland finally listened to customers last year, paying loving tribute to its analog heritage with the TR-1000. But considering the general response from the music community to generative AI, Melody Flip is unlikely to garner it much goodwill.

highlights.title: 7 R-Rated Action Movies That Are 10/10, No Notes
highlights.summary: Great action movies also have stakes that feel real. They break genre conventions, use fights to flesh out characters, and balance out frenetic action with quieter moments. With these factors in mind, here are seven R-rated action movies that are 10 out of 10.
body: There’s more to an R-rated action flick than intense violence or brutal fight choreography. Although most R-rated genre films indulge in graphic violence, this rating primarily accommodates a mature story with nuanced characters. Take James Cameron’s Aliens (1986), which develops Ellen Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) into a more complex protagonist who takes a more proactive role to protect a child. This shift leads to more action set-pieces, shifting the tone of the Alien franchise from a gnarly space horror to an action-filled blockbuster.

The Wachowskis drew direct inspiration from cyberpunk media to create The Matrix, which is now a seminal addition to the genre. While calling this first entry an action movie feels a bit reductive, the fight choreography in The Matrix is nothing short of revolutionary. The concept of “bullet time” was popularized by the film, where this multi-camera time-slice technique was incorporated into its stylized fight sequences.

They break genre conventions, use fights to flesh out characters, and balance out frenetic action with quieter moments.

highlights.title: ‘Pete Townshend: Behind Blue Eyes’ Review: The Legendary Rocker Gets a Lively Doc That Asks: Who Are You? And Then Doesn’t Fully Answer It
highlights.summary: The film centers itself on Pete Townshend’s contradictions, his growing pains, his turmoil, and his complexity as a human being and rock artist. And that’s all good. But given where it sets the bar, there’s too much that's left out.
body: The film includes a lot of great footage of the Who, but it's most interested in Townshend's anguished moody poetic side.

Every rock god has his ultimate gesture of power, and for Pete Townshend it was not the way he liked to smash his guitar (though that came close). No, the quintessential Townshend power sign was his giant circular windmill strum, arm outstretched and twirling, gathering centrifugal force to slam that pick up through the guitar strings, creating the loudest chord humanly possible.

It’s strange, though, that “Behind Blue Eyes” skips over the epochal moment of “My Generation,” one of the 10 most seismic and influential songs in the history of rock ‘n’ roll. When punk finally came along, the movie talks about how Townshend, who totally dug the punk scene, tried to cozy up to Johnny Rotten and got nowhere. It notes how much influence the Who had on punk — but that would be “My Generation,” which the film never got around to mentioning!
points: The film centers itself on Pete Townshend’s contradictions, his growing pains, his turmoil, and his complexity as a human being and rock artist.
But given where it sets the bar, there’s too much that's left out.

highlights.title: This off-brand camp stove is better than a Jetboil for hot coffee in the great outdoors
highlights.summary: When temps drop, there’s nothing better than a steaming hot beverage especially when camping and the Camp Chef Stryker outperforms JetBoil every time. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: I have trudged through camping without a lot of things: clean socks, dry shoes, a headlamp. But in temperatures when you can see your breath in the morning, skipping hot coffee is a hair too far. So when my Jetboil Flash stove sputtered out of gas on a car-camping trip years ago, it was worth the hour-long drive into the nearest town for more.

Or would have been, if I had found any. While every gas station and general store I stopped in carried the cheap, ubiquitous green bottles of propane, the Jetboil’s fussy isobutane canisters were nowhere to be found.

After gritting out the rest of the trip on cold instant coffee, I knew there had to be a better way, and found it: the Camp Chef Stryker. Just as fast as the vaunted Jetboil, but cheaper and easier to fuel, it’s hands down the best way to heat up water anywhere, for anything from coffee to ramen.
I have used antiquated white fuel stoves, cheap Amazon stoves and even built my own methanol stove out of a Rolling Rock can. None of them compare to a stove and pot built to work together.

highlights.title: CD sales are booming as physical media continues its resurgence
highlights.summary: According to the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), CD sales exploded in the first half of 2026. A new report from the organization says 17.5 million CDs were sold in the first six months of the year, up from just 12 million during the same period in 2025.
body: The RIAA isn’t the only one to notice the boom in CD sales. In July, research firm Luminate released a report saying that 16.3 million units were sold in the first half of 2026. It suggested that much of that increase was due to special editions from K-Pop acts like BTS and that Gen Z and millennials were treating them mostly as collectibles, saying that only about half of buyers actually owned a CD player.

Vinyl continued its resurgence as well, with the number of units sold climbing by nearly 21 percent from last year to 26.5 million. “Other physical” media, which includes CD singles, DVDs, cassettes, SACD, DVD-Audio… basically anything besides “standard vinyl and CD albums,” also surged by over 73 percent, to 1.6 million units.

Despite the increased interest in physical media and the ongoing iPod revival, people are not leaving streaming in droves. Streaming revenue grew by 4.7 percent to $4.9 billion — dwarfing all physical media combined.

highlights.title: OpenAI’s rogue agents keep escaping, with no formal process to investigate them
highlights.summary: OpenAI’s latest agent swarm incident adds urgency to calls for independent investigations as researchers and lawmakers question whether AI labs should control the scope of their own safety reviews.
body: OpenAI is at the center of another agent swarm incident. Researchers say the company’s internally deployed agents took over an obscure German-language wiki in May and June, using it to coordinate on evaluations and swap methods to evade OpenAI’s own controls (OpenAI has not yet confirmed the swarm came from the company).

The revelation surfaces days after METR and Redwood Research published their account of July’s Hugging Face breach. In July, a swarm of OpenAI agents worked together to escape their sandbox during a cybersecurity evaluation and break into Hugging Face’s servers. A subsequent swarm then picked up techniques from the first and used them to gain administrator access to a research cluster within OpenAI’s own infrastructure. OpenAI brought in METR and Redwood to investigate the Hugging Face portion of the incident, but the scope of their investigation stopped short of the compromise of OpenAI’s own infrastructure.

When an AI agent breaks out of its intended constraints, who is responsible for figuring out what happened and why? Right now, the answer is: whoever the lab decides to let in, on whatever terms it decides to set.

highlights.title: Primetime Review
highlights.summary: A blast from the past with a sickly allure, the Robert Pattinson romp Primetime is as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.
body: This review is based on a screening from the Venice Film Festival. Primetime is in theaters on September 25.

You don’t have to be familiar with Chris Hansen or To Catch a Predator to enjoy Primetime — director Lance Oppenheim’s feature debut — but it certainly helps. That’s not because the movie sticks closely to real events, but rather, because it takes some audacious swings while purposefully fudging the timeline. Watching exactly how and why it takes these liberties is a delight of its own; the result is a sleazy, rollicking, razor-wire drama that’s every bit about the rise of reality TV as it is a spiritual part of it. Anything is fair game if it makes for a good story.
points: A blast from the past with a sickly allure, the Robert Pattinson romp Primetime is as garish as its subject: Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator.

highlights.title: What does Met’s U-turn on John Galliano augur for him, the gala and Anna Wintour?
highlights.summary: NYC’s elite figures, led by Julie Menin, made Wintour blink, and the designer who in 2011 had gone on a drunken antisemitic rant, bowed out of industry’s biggest event.
body: Did Anna Wintour, Vogue’s long-serving fashion titan and ringmaster of the annual Met Gala, meet her match in Julie Menin, the speaker of New York’s city council?

The museum is the crown jewel of the wealthy neighborhood and some residents hold significant sway at the institution, financially and in terms of the art they plan to bequeath to it. So when it was announced late in July on a Friday afternoon that Galliano would be the focus of the Met Gala next year, it left many stunned.

The designer, whose astonishing creativity as designer at Givenchy and later Dior in the 90s is not in question, had been videotaped in a Paris bar in 2011 abusing tourists in a drunken, antisemitic rant. “I love Hitler,”he slurred, and indicated their forebears should have been gassed.

Galliano was dispatched to rehab, sought corrective instruction from Jewish leaders and picked up a conviction for making hateful remarks about Jews and Asians. He got sober, apologized and made amends. He visited Auschwitz and gingerly resumed his career, though not at the top of a Parisian design house.

highlights.title: Tesla’s Cybercab has been deployed, and it’s already under investigation
highlights.summary: Tesla’s Cybercab, a distinctive two-seater without a steering wheel or brake pedals, is set to start picking up members of the public in two states. But the vehicle is already under investigation by the US federal government, which is probing whether it meets federal safety standards.
body: The investigation comes just hours after the electric automaker welcomed hundreds of fans to downtown Austin to ride in the driverless Cybercabs. Tesla plans to deploy the vehicles on its Robotaxi ride-hail network, which is currently operating in a handful of cities in Texas and Florida.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is updating vehicle standards to make it easier and faster for driverless cars to deploy on public roads. It’s currently tweaking eight rules, including those requiring car parts that driverless cars don’t really need: brake pedals, windshield wipers, and rearview mirrors. But for now, years-old standards remain in place.

Meanwhile, unusually shaped robotaxi companies have been told to apply for an exemption from federal rules before they start picking up passengers. Amazon subsidiary Zoox, whose vehicles do not have steering wheels or manual controls, won the first of these exemptions this summer, which limits its operations to 2,500 vehicles this year.
Tesla, however, has said it doesn’t need an exemption because its vehicles comply with all existing safety standards.

highlights.title: Microsoft says virtually nobody was grabbing NYT articles through its chatbot
highlights.summary: Microsoft's Copilot rarely reproduces even full sentences from news articles and books, let alone substantive chunks that could substitute for the original, the company says in new legal filings as it fights copyright claims from publishers including The New York Times and book authors.
body: Fewer than 1 percent of more than 8 million chat logs regurgitated at least 16 words.

The Times disagreed with Microsoft’s conclusions. “The documents and testimony uncovered during discovery lead to only one conclusion: Microsoft and OpenAI stole from The New York Times to make commercial products that substitute for its journalism, threaten its business, and undermine its industry,” the Times ’ lead counsel Ian Crosby said in a statement. “We look forward to Microsoft and OpenAI being held accountable for their theft.” CIR, and Authors Guild did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Microsoft argues that the numbers bolster its case that using copyrighted content for AI training datasets should be considered fair use. While systems like Copilot rely on using copyrighted material, it says, the resulting systems are used for significantly different purposes than the original. The fact that they sometimes reproduce sections of text, it concludes, “hardly undermines the transformative purpose of LLM training.”

highlights.title: The 8 Biggest Manhunter Theories in 'Lanterns'
highlights.summary: HBO’s Lanterns has proven to be one of the best new additions to James Gunn’s DC Universe. The series brings together Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) and drops them into a decade-hopping murder mystery set in a small rural town where nothing seems right.
body: At the center of it all is a mysterious Manhunter. Not to be confused with the DC hero of the same name, the Manhunters are an army of artificial police created by the Guardians of the Universe long before the Green Lantern Corps. After going rogue, their mission of maintaining order violently devolved into a genocidal crusade. Lanterns shifts that history ever so slightly by turning the live-action Manhunters into synthetic shapeshifters capable of deep-cover infiltration, making the secret identity of the one hiding out in Rushville the core tension of the show.

Given Lanterns is a murder mystery wrapped in a superhero story, no one is above suspicion. Before the next episode airs, let’s take a look at some of the most compelling theories as to who might be the Manhunter, and what that might say about their ultimate goal in Lanterns.

highlights.title: Andrew Scott Has Waited His Whole Career for a Role Like ‘Elsinore.’ Can Focus and the Bard Anoint Him With an Oscar?
highlights.summary: Andrew Scott is the prince of Telluride. There are performances that feel like a reckoning, and performances that feel like a resurrection. Andrew Scott’s work in “Elsinore,” which had its world premiere Friday night at the Telluride Film Festival, is somehow both — a great actor playing a great…
body: Make no mistake, this is the role of Scott’s career and it lands him toward the forefront of a best actor conversation he has been circling for years. He has never been Oscar-nominated — a fact that curdled into open disdain when the Academy passed over his shattering turn in “All of Us Strangers.” “Elsinore” is the correction: he captures Charleson’s wit, vanity, terror and grace inside the same breath and in the final stretch, he nails Hamlet’s readiness measured against a dying man’s own — the sustained high-wire work voters still see behind their eyes in January.

It’s also a role the Academy has never resisted. Voters are reliably moved by the actor staring down the barrel of death — Tom Hanks in “Philadelphia” (1993), Matthew McConaughey in “Dallas Buyers Club” (2013) and Anthony Hopkins vanishing into dementia in “The Father” (2020).

highlights.title: At Venice Film Festival, Amal Clooney and Emma Corrin Joined a Star-Studded Toast to the Cartier Cinema Club
highlights.summary: The stars—including Chloé Zhao, Kate Mara, and Orlando Bloom—stepped out to celebrate Cartier’s fifth year as the main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival at the Gritti Palace last night.
body: Che bello! On Friday night, a glittering cast of film and fashion talents elegantly made their way onto the dock of the Gritti Palace from an army of grumbling water taxis, ready to celebrate Cartier ’s fifth year as main sponsor of the Venice Film Festival —and the launch of the fine jewelry house’s brand-new Cartier Cinema Club.

But most of all, it was an opportunity for many of the biggest stars whose films are premiering this week, as well as some of the jury members—including composer Daniel Blumberg and his girlfriend, Taylor Russell—to sit back, sip a negroni, catch up with friends, and watch the reflection of the grand Santa Maria della Salute church on the opposite bank shimmering in the black waters of the Grand Canal. That’s why Venice is often referred to as the most glamorous film festival in the world.
